hypotheses.statement: Let $\mathcal B/S$ be smooth and locally of finite type, and let $\mathscr U/S$ be a smooth curve of allowed legs.
Let $F\in D_{\mathrm{lcc}}(\mathcal B)$ be a Hecke eigencomplex with lisse eigenvalues.
In the trait case, assume $\Psi F=0$.

Let $X/\mathbb C$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus at least two, with $s\geq2$ distinct marked points, divisor $D$ their sum, and $G=\mathrm{SL}_n$.
Let $\sigma$ be a continuous dense $\check G$-parameter on their complement, defined over a finite coefficient extension, with unipotent monodromy at every marking.

The parameter $\rho$ lifts to a continuous parameter $\rho_{K_0}:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathscr U_{K_0})\to\check G(L)$ with the same compact image. After compatible choices of boundary fibers and prime-to-$p$ roots of unity, its full inertia homomorphism at $\mathfrak x_i$ is $$\label{lift:inertia} \rho_{K_0}(\gamma)=\exp\bigl(t_{\ell,i}(\gamma)N_i\bigr).$$ In particular every other prime factor of characteristic-zero inertia acts trivially. Its lattice reductions extend lisse over $\mathscr U$ and specialize to those of $\rho$, with the tensor compatibilities of Proposition 4.

outputs.exact_statement: For every parameter [intro:parameter] satisfying the preceding hypotheses, there is a nonzero locally constructible perverse geometric $E$-adic sheaf $M$ on $\mathcal A$ with $$\relax(M)\subset\Lambda_D.$$ For every finite set $I$ and every family $(V_i)_{i\in I}$, it has isomorphisms $$\label{intro:eigen} \mathop{\mathrm{Hecke}}_{I,(V_i)}(M) \simeq M\boxtimes\Bigl(\mathop{\boxtimes}_{i\in I}(V_i)_\rho\Bigr) \qquad\text{on }\mathcal A\times U^I,$$ natural in the representations and coherent for the tensor unit, convolution, permutations, and fusion on every collision diagonal. These isomorphisms use the relative normalization above.

For a smooth finite-type chart $S\to\mathcal B$ of pure dimension $d$, $$\dim\Lambda_S\le d.$$ In characteristic zero the cone is isotropic: the symplectic form vanishes on the smooth locus of every reduced subvariety of $\Lambda_S$.

If $a(t)\in\mathfrak{sl}_n[[t]]$ and $a(0)$ is not nilpotent, then, after a change of formal $\mathrm{SL}_n$-frame, there are a block Levi $M$ and a cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbb G_m\to Z(M)$ such that $$\label{geom:normal-form}
 a(t)\in\mathfrak m[[t]],\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{ad}}(a(0))|_{\mathfrak g/\mathfrak m}\text{ is invertible},\qquad
                    \kappa(a(0),d\lambda)\ne0.$$

For a geometric covector $A\in T_b^*\mathcal B\setminus\Lambda$, there are an allowed leg $y$, such an $H$, a point $h$ with $p(h)=b$ and $l(h)=y$, a covector $A'\in T^*_{o(h)}\mathcal B$, and $0\ne\xi\in T_y^*U$ with $$\label{geom:identity}
                         p^*A=q_H^*(A',\xi)\quad\text{at }h.$$ The following sections have nondegenerate zeros at $h$:*

1.  *on $H_{\mathrm{in}}=\widetilde p^{-1}(b,y)$, the restriction of $p^*A$ to the $q_H$-vertical tangent bundle;*

2.  *on $H_{\mathrm{out}}=q_H^{-1}(o(h),y)$, the restriction of $o^*A'$ to the $\widetilde p$-vertical tangent bundle.*

*Each restriction is a section of the dual of the indicated vertical tangent bundle. The fibers include the identifications of the fixed bundles; these fibers and the vertical tangent bundles have dimension and rank $m$, respectively. The point $y$ can be chosen in any prescribed nonempty open of a component on which $A$ is not generically nilpotent.

Let $F\in D_{\mathrm{lcc}}(\mathcal B)$ be a Hecke eigencomplex with lisse eigenvalues. In the product and quotient cases assume the eigenrelations on both open curves. Then, for every smooth finite-type chart $b:S\to\mathcal B$, $$\relax(b^*F)\subset\Lambda_S.$$ For this conclusion it is enough to have the individual one-leg isomorphisms $\mathop{\mathrm{Hecke}}_V(F)\simeq F\boxtimes\mathcal V_V$ for all Satake representations $V$, with each $\mathcal V_V$ lisse; their coherence is not needed in this section.

In this relative setup, let $F\in D_{\mathrm{lcc}}(\mathcal B_{\bar\eta})$ be a Hecke eigencomplex with lisse eigenvalues on $L_{\bar\eta}$ satisfying the lattice specialization condition of Proposition 3. If $\Psi F=0$, then on every smooth finite-type chart $D\to\mathcal B$ the closure of the generic nonzero-stalk locus of $F|_{D_{\bar\eta}}$ does not meet $D_s$.

If the differential $df_d$ in the field case, respectively its relative special-fiber differential in the trait case, lies outside $\Lambda_D$, then $$(\Phi_f K)_d=0
      \quad\text{in the field case},\qquad
      \bigl(\Psi(K|_{\{f=0\}_{\bar\eta}})\bigr)_d=0
      \quad\text{in the trait case}.$$ Here $\Phi_f$ is the unshifted cone from restriction to geometric nearby cycles for $f$.

In the trait case, assume $\Psi F=0$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ vanish at $d\in D_s$ and suppose their special-fiber differentials span an $r$-dimensional subspace $V\subset T_d^*D_s$ with $V\cap(\Lambda_D)_d=\{0\}$. Then nearby cycles of $K|_{\{f_1=\cdots=f_r=0\}_{\bar\eta}}$ vanish at $d$. The statement for $r=0$ is $\Psi K=0$.

Suppose $F\in D_{\mathrm{lcc}}(\mathcal B,E)$ is a coherent Hecke eigencomplex for a continuous parameter $\sigma:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U)\to\check G(L)$ with Zariski-dense image, where $L/\mathbb Q_\ell$ is finite. Then every ${}^pH^j(F)$ has a natural coherent eigenstructure for $\sigma$, with singular support in $\Lambda$. The eigenmaps are natural in representations and compatible with the unit, convolution, permutations, and fusion on every collision diagonal. If $F\ne0$, some ${}^pH^j(F)$ is nonzero. No global cohomological bound on $F$ and no condition on the boundary monodromy are required.

Let $K\in\mathscr D_\Lambda(\mathcal B)$ have a coherent Betti eigenstructure with parameter represented by $y\in Y(E)$. Every $f\in E[Y]^{\check G}$ acts, as a degree-zero endomorphism of the spectral unit and hence of $K$, by $f(y)\operatorname{id}_K$.

If the entries of $y\in Y(E)$ generate a Zariski-dense subgroup of $\check G=\mathrm{PGL}_{n,E}$, then for every nonzero representation $V$, of dimension $b$, there are an invariant $f_V\in E[Y]^{\check G}$ with $f_V(y)\ne0$ and equivariant maps $$\alpha_V:\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus b}\longrightarrow\mathscr E_V,
 \qquad
 \beta_V:\mathscr E_V\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus b}$$ such that $$\label{perv:adjugates}
 \beta_V\alpha_V=f_V\operatorname{id},\qquad
 \alpha_V\beta_V=f_V\operatorname{id}.$$
The subcategory $\mathscr D_S$ is preserved by perverse truncations and by all fixed-point Hecke functors. Every fixed-point Hecke functor is perverse $t$-exact on this subcategory.
If $Q\in D_{\mathrm{lcc}}(\mathcal A^+,E)$ has nilpotent singular support, its Betti realization is monodromic along the whole $T^s$-torsor $q$, and along each enhancement separately.

Let $P\xrightarrow{\pi}C\xrightarrow{b}Y$ be a factorization over an analytic disc $\Delta$, with $\pi$ a torus torsor on the entire family and $b$ proper. On finite-dimensional paracompact charts suppose that $F$ over $\Delta^*$ is weakly constructible and relatively monodromic along $\pi$. Then the natural exchange $$\label{desc:push-exchange}
            \Psi(b\pi)_*F\longrightarrow(b_0\pi_0)_*\Psi F$$ is an isomorphism. Base change and projection formula for these pushforwards also hold, and the comparisons respect composition. Here $\Psi$ denotes geometric Betti nearby cycles, without taking monodromy invariants.

Let $\sigma$ be a continuous Zariski-dense geometric adic parameter on $U$, defined over a finite coefficient extension, with unipotent local monodromy at every $x_i$. If $\mathcal A^+$ carries a nonzero lcc geometric adic coherent Hecke eigencomplex for $\sigma$, then $\mathcal A$ carries a nonzero locally constructible perverse geometric adic Hecke eigensheaf for $\sigma$. It has all the unit, convolution, permutation, and fusion compatibilities of Definition 2, and nilpotent singular support. No boundary monodromy is required to be regular.

(). *Let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $G$ be simple and simply connected. A continuous $\widehat G$-local system $\tau$ on $C$, defined over a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_\ell$ and with Zariski-dense image, admits a nonzero locally bounded constructible geometric $E$-adic eigencomplex on $\mathop{\mathrm{Bun}}_G(C)$. Its Hecke eigenstructure has the relative Satake normalization and is coherent for all finite sets of legs, including collision maps.

Put $K_1=\overline{\mathbb C((z))}$ and let $C_{K_1}$ be the smooth geometric generic curve. There is a continuous unramified parameter $\rho_{K_1}$ on $C_{K_1}$ with the same compact image as $\rho_1$. Its lattice reductions specialize on $U_1\sqcup U_2$ to those of $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$, with the tensor compatibilities of Proposition 4.

Let $X/\mathbb C$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus at least two, with $s\geq2$ distinct marked points, divisor $D$ their sum, and $G=\mathrm{SL}_n$. Let $\sigma$ be a continuous dense $\check G$-parameter on their complement, defined over a finite coefficient extension, with unipotent monodromy at every marking. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Bun}}_{G,B,D}(X)$ carries a nonzero locally constructible perverse geometric $E$-adic eigensheaf with eigenvalue $\sigma$, nilpotent singular support, and the full coherent Hecke system in relative Satake normalization.

The parameter $\rho$ lifts to a continuous parameter $\rho_{K_0}:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathscr U_{K_0})\to\check G(L)$ with the same compact image. After compatible choices of boundary fibers and prime-to-$p$ roots of unity, its full inertia homomorphism at $\mathfrak x_i$ is $$\label{lift:inertia} \rho_{K_0}(\gamma)=\exp\bigl(t_{\ell,i}(\gamma)N_i\bigr).$$ In particular every other prime factor of characteristic-zero inertia acts trivially. Its lattice reductions extend lisse over $\mathscr U$ and specialize to those of $\rho$, with the tensor compatibilities of Proposition 4.
